title: Maintaining IV Patency Throughout Pharmacokinetic Studies Through a Needle-Free Blood Draw Device.
abstract: 8 8 9 Pharmacokinetic (PK) studies require temporally precise measurements of drug concentrations in biological matrices, most commonly whole blood or plasma. However, repeated venous sampling may increase participant burden and complicate PK-intensive study designs. Needle-free blood collection devices that access peripheral intravenous (IV) catheters may provide an alternative approach to repeated venipuncture while maintaining sampling schedules and specimen quality. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of integrating the PIVO Pro needle-free blood collection device into a PK-intensive human laboratory study of inhaled Δ-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ-THC), Δ-THC, and placebo. Participants completed a screening visit and three dosing visits conducted in a university research facility equipped with a full-scale driving simulator. During each dosing visit, venous blood samples were collected at nine time points over approximately 8 h through an indwelling peripheral IV catheter using the PIVO device. All participants reported that study procedures, including blood collection, were acceptable. Approximately 40% of vascular access sites required replacement, most commonly within the first hour and typically associated with poor initial blood return. Despite slower flow compared with standard venipuncture, sampling was generally sufficient to maintain the PK sampling schedule. One mild adverse event related to vascular access (localized bruising) was observed. These findings demonstrate the operational feasibility of needle-free blood collection through indwelling IV catheters in a PK-intensive research protocol conducted outside a traditional clinical research unit. Further studies are warranted to compare analytical performance and access durability relative to conventional venous sampling approaches.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

title: Prophylactic Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Standard Wound Care Among Lower Extremity Amputations: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: P P Prophylactic closed incisional negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce postoperative wound complications following lower extremity amputation in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether closed incisional NPWT reduces wound complications compared with standard wound care (SWC) in this high-risk vasculopathic population. A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2025 using predefined search strings. Six studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models as the primary analysis to account for anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Leave-one-out analyses and an analysis excluding the study in which NPWT was delivered as part of a multifaceted care bundle were performed to assess robustness. A total of 893 patients were included, including 408 in the closed incisional NPWT group and 485 in the SWC group. Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) (OR = 0.370; 95% CI = 0.143-0.957; = .044) and wound dehiscence (OR = 0.224; 95% CI = 0.125-0.401; = .008). Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative SSI and wound dehiscence following lower extremity amputation in patients with PAD. Because the evidence is predominantly observational and prediction intervals included the null value, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered randomized trials.

title: Approach to the patient with elevated lipoprotein(a).
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a common, genetically determined lipoprotein that is independently associated with myocardial infarction, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and calcific aortic stenosis. Because Lp(a) levels are stable over time and minimally influenced by lifestyle, the 2026 ACC/AHA/Multisociety Dyslipidemia Guideline now recommends one-time measurement in all adults and cascade screening in high-risk families; as a result, endocrinologists can expect to encounter and manage elevated Lp(a) frequently in routine clinical practice. Despite its clinical importance, no approved drug therapies specifically targeting Lp(a) yet exist; therefore, management should currently focus on aggressive optimization of traditional risk factors, particularly LDL-C lowering with statins and selective use of adjunctive therapies such as PCSK9 inhibitors and lipid apheresis. Emerging evidence suggests a potential benefit of selective aspirin use, while novel therapeutics-antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNAs-which robustly lower Lp(a) are currently being tested in phase 3 clinical trials. We present case-based examples to highlight practical approaches to risk assessment and management of elevated Lp(a).

title: Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury in the Geriatric Population: Results from the Aortic Trauma Foundation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) is evolving as the trauma population ages, yet the impact of age on treatment patterns and outcomes remains incompletely defined. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective analysis of the Aortic Trauma Foundation registry (November 2016 to November 2023) identified 823 patients with BTAI, including 118 geriatric patients (65 years and older). Demographics, injury characteristics, management strategies, and outcomes were compared between the geriatric and younger (younger than 65 years) cohorts. RESULTS: Geriatric patients more frequently presented after falls (17.8% vs 6.7%, p < 0.0001) and had a higher proportion of grade IV injuries (18.5% vs 9.2%, p = 0.0021), with no difference in admission systolic blood pressure (116 vs 116, p = 0.960) or Injury Severity Score (31 vs 33, p = 0.150). Management strategies were similar between groups, including nonoperative (37.3% vs 36.9%, p = 0.932), open (4.2% vs 1.9%, p = 0.132), and endovascular repair (58.5% vs 61.1%, p = 0.584). Despite comparable treatment approaches, geriatric patients had higher in-hospital mortality (27.1% vs 10.9%, p < 0.0001) and aortic-related mortality (8.5% vs 3.4%, p = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: Geriatric patients with BTAI sustain more severe injuries and experience significantly higher mortality despite similar management strategies. These findings suggest that current treatment paradigms may not adequately address age-associated risk and highlight the need for age-specific management considerations.

title: Targeting Nupr1-Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b-Dependent Survival Program.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive. By integrating clinical observations and single-cell RNA sequencing, we found that Nuclear Protein 1 (Nupr1), a critical stress-responsive factor, is significantly upregulated in aortas from AD patients and murine models, with enrichment in VSMCs. Remarkably, VSMC-specific Nupr1 deficiency significantly ameliorated AD progression in vivo. Mechanistically, Nupr1 undergoes massive mitochondrial accumulation in Ang II-induced apoptotic VSMCs. Rather than operating as a conventional transcriptional regulator, mitochondrially enriched Nupr1 functions as a pathological spatial switch. It sequesters p53 within mitochondria, driving transcription-independent apoptosis while simultaneously blunting the protective Gadd45b-mediated survival program. Furthermore, in vivo Gadd45b overexpression was sufficient to rescue mitochondrial dysfunction and ameliorate vascular collapse. Taken together, our findings conceptualize the Nupr1-p53-Gadd45b axis as an important determinant of VSMC fate and provide a novel and promising therapeutic strategy for preventing AD progression.

title: Optimizing pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis in medical inpatients using sequential IMPROVE risk assessment models: Clinical, economic and environmental implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients. Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discrepancy between real-world thromboprophylaxis prescribing and a prespecified sequential IMPROVE-based strategy and assess its economic and environmental implications. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in internal medicine over one month. Adults hospitalized for>48h were included, excluding those receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. IMPROVE VTE and Bleeding scores were calculated retrospectively. Pharmacologic prophylaxis was supported by the strategy for patients with an IMPROVE Bleeding score<7 and IMPROVE VTE score≥2. Observed prescriptions were compared with the prespecified strategy using contingency analysis and Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: 2 Among 99 patients, 79.8% received pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, whereas 46.5% met the strategy criteria. Among treated patients, 46.8% did not meet these criteria. Strict application of the strategy would theoretically result in 292 fewer doses over one month, corresponding to €233.60 in estimated savings and approximately 405kg COeq. CONCLUSION: Real-world prescribing differed substantially from the prespecified strategy. Strict application would theoretically reduce anticoagulant use, costs, and carbon emissions. However, clinical outcomes were not assessed, and RAMs should complement rather than replace clinical judgment. Prospective studies incorporating VTE and bleeding outcomes are required to assess the safety of this approach.

title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease Without Dedicated Guidelines.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms (SAAs) represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695) RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported. Primary patency of the treated segment was 100% (43/43), as no graft/segment thrombosis, occlusion, or flow-limiting stenosis occurred; secondary patency was 100% (43/43). Where a numeric follow-up duration could be extracted, mean follow-up was 8 months (range, 6-11 months) in the endovascular group (4/5 patients), 15 months (range, 2 weeks-4 years) in the open group (5/13 patients), and 15 months (range, 1-60 months) in the hybrid group (6/7 patients); a precise duration was not reported for the remaining patients. CONCLUSION: The available evidence demonstrates that both open and endovascular repair can achieve satisfactory short- and mid-term outcomes. However, patient selection, procedural planning, and surveillance protocols remain poorly standardized. The observed recurrences and the limited duration of follow-up reported in the literature underscore the need for rigorous, lifelong surveillance. Prospective multicenter registries are warranted to refine best practice and to guide the development of devices and techniques tailored to fragile connective-tissue vessels.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute Type A aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD. METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to Zone 0/Zone 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (Zone 1-3) (complete 56% vs. incomplete/LTF 27%, p<0.001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs. incomplete/LTF 18%, p<0.001), in-hospital TEVAR extension (7% vs. 2%, p=0.028), and TEVAR extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs. incomplete/LTF 5%, p=0.002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete: 12% vs. incomplete: 5%, p=0.007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs. 15%, p=0.002) within 1-year of acute dissection. Long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete: 97% vs. incomplete: 97% vs. LTF: 91%), 3-years (complete: 92% vs. incomplete: 95% vs. LTF: 81%, p=0.021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (p=0.13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.1-3.9). CONCLUSION: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and mid-term survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.

title: Efficacy and Safety of No Thromboprophylaxis after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent Saphenous VeiNs: the TRAIN Non-inferiority Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The benefit of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after endovenous radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for incompetent saphenous veins in patients without previous deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the lower limbs is unclear. This trial compared no extended thromboprophylaxis with extended anticoagulation after RFA. METHODS: TRAIN (Thromboprophylaxis after endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent saphenous veiNs) was a multicentre, evaluator blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial. Adults with primary great saphenous vein incompetence undergoing RFA, with concomitant tributary phlebectomy and or ultrasound guided foam sclerotherapy when clinically indicated, were enrolled. Patients with previous DVT of the lower limbs were excluded. All participants received a single intra-operative intravenous dose of unfractionated heparin and were randomised to either no extended pharmacological thromboprophylaxis or rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for fourteen days post-operatively. The primary outcome was thrombosis related events within thirty days. RESULTS: Of 406 patients screened, 354 were included in the intention to treat analysis and 304 in the per protocol analysis. The no extended thromboprophylaxis strategy was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events (risk difference -1.34%, 95% confidence interval -7.53 - 4.84%; p = .022 for non-inferiority). One participant in the anticoagulation group (one of 177; 0.6%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding on post-operative day 10. No bleeding event occurred in the no anticoagulation group (0 of 177; p = 1.0). CONCLUSION: Omitting extended post-operative rivaroxaban thromboprophylaxis after RFA with concomitant phlebectomy and sclerotherapy in patients without previous DVT was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events. Prophylactic rivaroxaban was not associated with an increased risk of bleeding.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA prior to DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs. 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use Before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) are increasingly prescribed for glycemic control and weight management, but their association with postoperative thrombotic events after total knee arthroplasty remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using deidentified data from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including adults who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty between December 1, 2006 and June 1, 2025. Patients with prior myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, venous thromboembolism, or pulmonary embolism were excluded. Exposure was defined as a prescription for a GLP-1 RA within 1 year and 1 day before surgery. A 1:1 propensity score match was performed on demographics, relevant comorbidities, and medications, yielding 11,765 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were postoperative myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, venous thromboembolism, and pulmonary embolism. Compared with matched controls, patients prescribed GLP-1 receptor agonists had a significantly lower risk of myocardial infarction (25/11,246 vs 47/11,171; risk ratio [RR] 0.528; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.325 - 0.858). GLP-1 RA use was also associated with a reduced risk of deep vein thrombosis (74/11,319 vs 103/11,308; RR 0.718; 95% CI, 0.533 - 0.966) and venous thromboembolism (133/11,040 vs 172/11,027; RR 0.772; 95% CI, 0.617 - 0.967). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of pulmonary embolism between groups (49/11,352 vs 58/11,382; RR 0.847; 95% CI, 0.580 - 1.238). Overall, preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a significantly lower postoperative risk of myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, and venous thromboembolism following total knee arthroplasty in this large, nationally representative cohort.

title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses. METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests. RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits. title: Lived experiences of post-traumatic growth in patients with acute type A aortic dissection: A qualitative study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute type A aortic dissection is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency characterized by sudden onset, severe pain, and high mortality, exerting profound physical and psychological burdens on affected individuals. While negative psychological sequelae predominate in most cases, a subset of patients demonstrates remarkable resilience, manifesting post-traumatic growth-a positive psychological transformation emerging in the aftermath of trauma. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the lived experiences of post-traumatic growth among Acute type A aortic dissection survivors, shedding light on this understudied dimension of their recovery trajectory. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted using a phenomenological approach. Twenty patients diagnosed with Acute type A aortic dissection were recruited through purposive sampling from a tertiary hospital in China. Data were collected via in-depth, face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method to extract key themes and sub-themes. RESULTS: Three overarching themes and eight sub-themes were identified, reflecting the multidimensional nature of post-traumatic growth in Acute type A aortic dissection patients: Reevaluating Life Priorities (reordering life priorities, valuing life), Behavioral Transformation (improving unhealthy habits, enhancing treatment adherence), and Enhanced Social Connections (strengthened family ties, gratitude for social support, reintegration into family and society, altruistic behavior). CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates three core dimensions of post-traumatic growth in survivors of acute type A aortic dissection: life priority reassessment, adoption of positive health behaviors, and enhanced social connectedness. The findings underscore the critical role of guided self-reflection, supported behavior change, and robust family-social support systems in facilitating psychological recovery. We recommend integrating interventions focused on post-traumatic growth, such as psychological counseling and structured family support, into standard cardiac rehabilitation protocols to promote holistic recovery. Together, these insights provide a theoretical and practical foundation for developing tailored psychosocial interventions for this patient population.

title: Impact of GLP-1 Agonists on Post-Operative Outcomes in Aesthetic & Body Contouring Surgery: A Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have rapidly expanded in use for weight loss, resulting in a growing population of patients presenting for aesthetic and body-contouring procedures. Despite their increasing prevalence, the effects of GLP-1 RAs on postoperative wound healing and surgical outcomes remain poorly defined. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from database inception through May 2026. Studies comparing postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing aesthetic and/or body-contouring surgery with and without GLP-1 RA exposure were included. Primary outcomes included infection, wound dehiscence, delayed wound healing, hypertrophic scarring, seroma, hematoma, and venous thromboembolism (VTE). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 29,357 patients met inclusion criteria, with 10 studies included in quantitative synthesis. In pooled observational analyses, GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with increased risk of delayed wound healing and hypertrophic scarring. Subgroup analysis comparing GLP-1 RA users with patients who had previously undergone bariatric surgery demonstrated decreased seroma rates in the GLP-1 RA group. CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 RA use in patients undergoing aesthetic and body-contouring surgery was associated in pooled observational analyses with increased risks of delayed wound healing and hypertrophic scarring, while GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower seroma rates in comparison with patients who have undergone bariatric surgery. As GLP-1 RA use become increasingly prevalent, further prospective studies are needed to clarify their perioperative effects and optimize patient selection and surgical outcomes.

title: Implementation of a Guideline-Based Preference Elicitation Tool to Enhance Shared Decision-Making in Supervised Exercise Therapy for Patients With Intermittent Claudication: A Multi-Methods Cluster Randomized Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Shared decision-making is not yet common practice in physical therapy, emphasizing the need for effective decision aids. A preference elicitation tool (PE-tool) was designed to complement supervised exercise therapy (SET) in intermittent claudication treatment. OBJECTIVE: Primarily, to assess the impact of implementing the PE-tool on patients' functional walking distance (FWD), maximal walking distance (MWD) and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) after 3 and 6 months. Secondarily, to assess the tool's impact on shared decision-making and person-centeredness. DESIGN: Nationwide pragmatic cluster randomized trial. SETTING: Primary care physical therapy practices in the Netherlands. PARTICIPANTS: Primary care physical therapists and patients with intermittent claudication receiving SET. EXPOSURE(S): Therapists assigned to the intervention group had access to the PE-tool to complement SET, whereas therapists in the control group delivered SET. MAIN OUTCOME(S) AND MEASURE(S): Group differences in FWD, MWD, and HRQoL at 3- and 6-month follow-ups were assessed using routinely collected clinical data. Audio-recorded consultations between therapists and patients in the intervention (n = 72) and control group (n = 74) were assessed using the OPTION-5 instrument to assess shared decision-making. Participating patients completed a questionnaire afterwards to assess person-centeredness. RESULTS: Intention-to-treat analyses indicated no statistically significant differences between intervention (n = 1199 patients) and control (n = 915 patients) groups at both follow-ups for FWD and MWD. For HRQoL, a statistically significant difference favoring the control group was found at 3-month follow-up (MD = -0.3 points), but not at 6-month (MD = -0.3 points). Statistically significant effects favoring the intervention group were found for shared decision-making (MD = +39.0 points) and person-centeredness (MD = +2.0 points). CONCLUSIONS: Use of the PE-tool in intermittent claudication treatment did not improve patient-level outcomes compared to SET alone, but positively impacted levels of shared decision-making and person-centeredness. RELEVANCE: Although achieving health improvements through decision aids remains complex, the novel tool could support therapists in adopting a more collaborative and person-centered approach.

title: Pulmonary embolism in shoulder arthroplasty: a National Joint Registry Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the UK, there is no specific guidance on prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism (VTE) following shoulder arthroplasty (SA). This study reviews the current incidence of pulmonary embolism (PE) and prophylaxis practices following SA in England. METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Joint Registry (NJR) for all SAs from 1 April 2012 to 31 March 2022 and linked with Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). ICD-10 codes identified incidence of PE at 30 and 90 days from arthroplasty. Incidence for PE was calculated by cohort and implant type at 30 and 90 days postoperatively. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated independently with PE. RESULTS: A total of 47,145 procedures were included in the NJR HES linked database; 26,403 reverse SAs (RSAs), 12,736 total SAs (TSAs) and 8,006 hemiarthroplasties (HAs). The cumulative incidence of PE was 0.25% at 30 days and 0.33% at 90 days. By implant type, the cumulative incidence was 0.32% following RSA, 0.15% following TSA and 0.18% following HA at 30 days, and 0.41%, 0.21% and 0.25%, respectively, at 90 days. Chemical VTE prophylaxis was received following 74.55% of procedures and mechanical prophylaxis following 96.27%. Most common chemical prophylaxis was low molecular weight heparin (91.34%). Congestive cardiac failure, peripheral vascular disease, metastatic disease and trauma indication were associated independently with PE. CONCLUSIONS: Although uncommon, PE remains an important postoperative complication given its associated morbidity and mortality. Despite most patients receiving some form of prophylaxis no agreed guidance exists in SA and further studies are needed to inform such guidance.

title: Percutaneous Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension in a High-Risk Real-World Population: Preliminary Results From a Prospective Single-Center Experience.
abstract: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system. All had baseline office systolic BP (SBP) > 155 mmHg and diastolic BP > 90 mmHg despite at least three antihypertensive drugs at the maximum tolerated doses. Clinical response required both an office SBP reduction ≥ 10 mm Hg and a mean 24-h ambulatory SBP reduction ≥ 5 mm Hg. Outcomes were assessed within 72 h and at 1 month. All procedures were technically successful. At 72 h, 15 patients (83.3%) met both response criteria; all had an office SBP reduction ≥ 20 mm Hg. At 1 month, 16 (88.9%) were responders and 2 (11.1%) were nonresponders. Among responders, five discontinued one drug and continued dual therapy, whereas 11 continued three drugs at reduced doses. Procedural events included one iatrogenic renal artery dissection, one femoral artery dissection with perforation, one guidewire fracture successfully retrieved with an endovascular snare, and two femoral hematomas. Renal function did not deteriorate. In conclusion, radiofrequency RDN was technically feasible and was followed by an early clinical response in most patients. The small sample, short follow-up, and absence of a control group preclude definitive efficacy conclusions.

title: Identification of perioperative risk factors for retrograde type A dissection after thoracic endovascular aortic repair for type B dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify risk factors and develop a predictive model for retrograde type A dissection (RTAD) following thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHODS: We analyzed TBAD patients who underwent TEVAR from 2014 to 2024 (IRB:No. TJ-IRB20230805). Patients developing RTAD within 1 year were matched with controls by age, sex, operation date, and location. Logistic regression identified risk factors, and a nomogram was constructed. Model performance was assessed using ROC curves. RESULTS: p p p p p p Of 2383 patients, 76 (3.19%) developed RTAD within one year. 65 RTAD cases and 195 matched controls were analyzed. RTAD patients had a greater horizontal distance of the ascending aorta (HDAA) than controls (53.34 mm vs. 43.05 mm, < .001). Multivariate analysis identified younger age (OR = 0.95, = .008), larger HDAA (OR = 1.14, < .001), aortic root dilatation (OR = 2.85, = .006), shorter stent length (OR = 0.99, = .029), and absence of postoperative bradycardic drug use (OR = 0.31, = .005) as independent RTAD risk factors. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.85). CONCLUSION: Younger age, larger HDAA, aortic root dilatation, shorter stent length, and no bradycardic drugs postoperatively are independent predictors of RTAD after TEVAR. For TBAD patients with a high risk of RTAD, clinicians should consider the possibility of having connective tissue diseases, select stents appropriately, and optimize postoperative treatment with strict follow-up.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Intraosseous Regional Versus Intravenous Tranexamic Acid in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) reduces perioperative blood loss in total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, evidence for intraosseous regional administration (IORA) remains limited. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of IORA-TXA versus intravenous TXA (IV-TXA) in TKA. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center trial, 98 patients undergoing primary TKA were randomized 1:1 to IORA-TXA or IV-TXA (49 per group) at a uniform dose of 20 mg/kg. The primary outcome was calculated perioperative blood loss. Secondary efficacy outcomes included calculated hidden blood loss, postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) levels, and transfusion rate. Safety outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular calf vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism (PE), and wound-related complications. RESULTS: Compared with IV-TXA, IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative blood loss (674.8 ± 335.0 vs. 817.5 ± 357.2 mL; mean difference, 142.6 mL; 95% CI, 7.4-277.8; p = 0.038) and calculated hidden blood loss (644.8 ± 335.5 vs. 790.9 ± 339.0 mL; mean difference, 146.1 mL; 95% CI, 10.9-281.3; p = 0.035). Postoperative Hb was similar on POD1 (134.0 ± 9.8 vs. 130.1 ± 11.1 g/L; p = 0.067) but was higher with IORA-TXA on POD2 (119.8 ± 8.3 vs. 113.8 ± 11.5 g/L; mean difference 6.0 g/L; 95% CI 2.0-10.0; p = 0.005) and POD3 (114.8 ± 7.9 vs. 109.8 ± 12.6 g/L; mean difference 5.0 g/L; 95% CI 0.8-9.2; p = 0.020). No patient required blood transfusion. DVT detected by routine postoperative Doppler occurred numerically more often with IORA-TXA than with IV-TXA: 10.2% (95% CI, 3.4%-22.2%) versus 0.0% (95% CI, 0.0%-7.3%); p = 0.056. CONCLUSIONS: IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative and hidden blood loss and improved early postoperative Hb preservation compared with IV-TXA. However, DVT incidence was numerically higher with IORA-TXA, indicating a potential thromboembolic safety signal that warrants confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials. title: Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation; results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis after pLT. METHODS: Our study analyzed data from the Portal vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers, across 18 countries, over a 20-year period. Graft- and patient survival rates were determined after PVS diagnosis. RESULTS: This study included 239 patients (53% female; median age at pLT 1.1 years) diagnosed with PVS. The median age at diagnosis was 2.7 years. The overall ten-year graft survival was 90%, and the ten-year patient survival was 96%. One-year graft and patient survival was lowest in patients with PVS diagnosed ≤7 days after pLT (80% and 92%, respectively). Initial treatment strategies comprised of mostly endovascular procedures (87%), followed by conservative (11%) and surgical treatment (3%). Patient outcome did not differ between these treatment groups. Within the endovascular group, graft survival in patients treated with stent (n=26) was significantly lower compared to those with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (n=181) (88% vs 98%, respectively, p=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.

title: Chronic Anticoagulation Increases Complications in Obliterative Prolapse Surgery.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Chronic anticoagulation has been identified as a risk factor for postoperative complications in other specialties, but there is a paucity of data on its effect on older women undergoing obliterative prolapse repair. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess whether chronic anticoagulation is associated with increased serious adverse events (SAEs) after obliterative prolapse surgery. STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort analysis of women 65 years or older undergoing obliterative prolapse repair at 2 academic institutions from 2016 to 2023. Patients were identified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code and grouped by preoperative chronic anticoagulation status. The composite primary outcome was defined as SAE within 8 weeks of surgery. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, controlling for relevant variables with P <0.10 on univariate analysis. RESULTS: Among the 777 older women who underwent obliterative surgery, 97 (12.5%) were chronically anticoagulated. The most commonly used anticoagulants were apixaban (n = 37, 38.1%) and clopidogrel (n = 31, 32%), with 21.7% reporting concomitant use of aspirin. Anticoagulated individuals were more likely to be current smokers and to have a history of venous thromboembolism, myocardial infarction, and stroke (P < 0.05). Chronically anticoagulated women had 1.72 times greater adjusted odds of experiencing SAE (95% CI, 1.02-2.91). Chronic anticoagulation was associated with an increased incidence of readmission, cardiac complications, transfusion, hematoma, and organ-space surgical site infection (P < 0.05). Rates of SAEs were highest in individuals taking rivaroxaban (35.7%) and those taking concomitant aspirin (38.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Chronic anticoagulation is associated with increased odds of SAE in older women undergoing obliterative prolapse surgery. Physicians should consider this additional risk in surgical decision making and counseling on anticoagulant suspension and resumption perioperatively.

title: Implementation of a multi-disciplinary hemodialysis access clinic improves time to surgical evaluation and access case volume.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Delays in hemodialysis access creation contribute to prolonged tunneled dialysis catheter dependence and morbidity. In March 2025, our institution implemented a multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic with weekly reserved appointments, same-day duplex vein mapping, and streamlined nephrology-to-surgery referral. We evaluated its effect on access volume, timing to surgical evaluation, and catheter dependence. METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of adults undergoing hemodialysis access procedures at a tertiary academic center from March 17, 2024 to March 13, 2026. Access volume was compared before and after implementation. Patient-level timing metrics were compared between patients evaluated in standard vascular surgery clinic versus multidisciplinary accelerated clinic. RESULTS: p p p p p p Mean monthly access volume increased from 3.08 ± 2.15 to 8.58 ± 3.00 cases after implementation, an increase of 5.5 cases per month ( < 0.001). Annual access volume increased from 37 to 103 cases ( < 0.001). Among 53 patients, 29 were evaluated in the standard clinic and 24 in the multidisciplinary clinic. Referral-to-clinic time decreased from 63.6 ± 47.7 to 41.0 ± 35.9 days ( = 0.01). Clinic-to-operation time did not differ significantly (21.8 ± 18.5 vs 27.1 ± 17.2 days; = 0.14). Overall referral-to-operation time decreased from 85.4 ± 51.5 to 68.2 ± 43.9 days but did not reach significance ( = 0.07). Catheter dependence was lower in the multidisciplinary cohort (29% vs 48%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.11-1.16). Same-day vein mapping was performed more frequently in the accelerated clinic cohort than in the standard clinic cohort (100% vs 51.7%, < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic increased procedural volume and shortened time to surgical evaluation. However, total time to access creation was not significantly reduced, suggesting that downstream operative capacity may remain an important barrier.

title: Comparison of arteriovenous fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis and haemodialysis: A matched case-control study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Arteriovenous fistulas constitute an effective vascular access option for haemodialysis, demonstrating high patency rates and lower infection risk compared with synthetic accesses. Treatment algorithms and patient characteristics differ between haemodialysis and apheresis therapy, and fistula outcomes in patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis have not yet been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study compared arteriovenous fistula outcomes in 29 patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis with those of 87 frequency-matched patients on haemodialysis. Matching criteria included age, sex, fistula configuration and diabetes mellitus status. Primary and secondary patency rates and associated risk factors were assessed over a 24-month follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: n n n n p p p p The study included patients with radiocephalic ( = 72) or brachiocephalic ( = 44) arteriovenous fistulas. Indications for apheresis were elevated lipoprotein(a) levels ( = 26) and dyslipoproteinemia ( = 3). Mean age was comparable between groups (61.4 vs 61.2 years), as was the proportion of male patients (58.6% vs 60.9%). Diabetes mellitus was present in 58.6% of apheresis patients and 49.4% of haemodialysis patients. Two-year primary patency rates were comparable between groups (49.2% vs 50.8%), while secondary patency was lower in the apheresis group (59.9% vs 71.1%). In the apheresis cohort, diabetes was associated with reduced primary (HR, 4.034; 95 % CI, 1.10-14.80; = 0.035) and secondary patency (HR, 9.807; 95 % CI, 1.24-77.59; = 0.030). Apheresis before fistula creation demonstrated improved secondary patency (HR, 0.198; 95% CI, 0.04-0.94; = 0.042). In haemodialysis patients, hyperlipoproteinemia was associated with reduced secondary patency (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.01-5.14; = 0.046). CONCLUSIONS: Arteriovenous fistula patency in patients undergoing apheresis was comparable to haemodialysis patients despite elevated lipoprotein levels. Diabetes was associated with reduced fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis. The findings support arteriovenous fistulas as long-term access option and highlight the importance of individualised access planning.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy Is Associated With Lower Risk of Lower Extremity Amputation in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes and Foot Ulcer Without Coded Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Hypothesis-Generating Real-World Cohort Study.
abstract: AIMS: To compare lower extremity amputation (LEA) risk in adults with Type 2 diabetes and diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) treated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) versus other glucose-lowering therapy, and to test whether coded peripheral arterial disease (PAD) modifies this association and replicates across comparator classes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user, active-comparator retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (queried 11 July 2026). Adults with Type 2 diabetes and DFU were propensity-score matched 1:1 on 22 covariates, giving 21 325 pairs for the primary comparison. Effect modification by coded PAD (ICD-10 I70.2) was examined in independently matched subgroups. Six sensitivity analyses were pre-specified: 30- and 180-day landmarks, all-cause mortality, background-therapy balancing, limb-severity adjustment and a broadened PAD definition. RESULTS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower 5-year LEA risk than all non-GLP-1 RA therapy (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.54-0.67). The association was confined to the no-PAD stratum (HR: 0.21, 0.13-0.33) and absent where PAD was coded (HR: 0.97, 0.78-1.20); ratio of hazard ratios 0.21 (0.13-0.36; p < 0.001). All-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.48, 0.45-0.50). The insulin no-PAD estimate persisted under background-therapy balancing (0.14), limb-severity adjustment (0.16) and 30- and 180-day landmarks (0.28, 0.33). Broadening the PAD definition attenuated the no-PAD association without abolishing it (HR: 0.34, 0.17-0.65). CONCLUSIONS: In Type 2 diabetes with DFU, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower LEA risk, surviving six pre-specified sensitivity analyses. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

title: "Not so minor" - Digital Amputation as a precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish tertiary vascular centre.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for five-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017-2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry (HIPE) data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least one minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (± 12.7). 70% had PAD and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n=73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major re-amputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischaemic heart disease (IHD) (OR 2.796, 95% CI 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136) and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularisation at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8% and 48% at one, three and five years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in PROSPERO, was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER. RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (OR, 2.58; 95% CI, 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%). CONCLUSIONS: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow-up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow-up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate to serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

title: Postoperative complications following carotid endarterectomy are differentially impacted by sex and plaque instability.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in post-carotid endarterectomy outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for carotid endarterectomy rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing carotid endarterectomy for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year post-surgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery. Additionally, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact post-endarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.

title: Endovascular Iliac Stenting versus Open Aortobifemoral Bypass for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischaemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative-effectiveness data adjusted for treatment-selection bias remain limited. This multicentre study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD. METHODS: Retrospective, non-randomised cohort study of 171 patients with AIOD (Rutherford 3-6) treated at three centres (UK, Ireland, Egypt) between January 2023 and February 2026. Outcomes were primary patency, freedom from reintervention (FFR), amputation-free survival (AFS), overall survival, and perioperative complications. Cox regression and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: 125 patients (73.1%) underwent endovascular treatment and 46 (26.9%) open bypass. Endovascular patients were older (66.8 vs 60.8 years, p<0.001) and had a lower burden of TASC C-D disease (53.6% vs 93.5%, p<0.001). Primary patency at 24 months was 62.7% vs 91.8% (log-rank p<0.001; IPTW-adjusted HR 5.67, 95% CI 1.75-18.37). Freedom from reintervention at 24 months was 63.1% vs 93.3% (p<0.001). Amputation-free survival (85.0% vs 87.4%, p=0.992) and overall survival (93.3% vs 90.0%, p=0.335) were comparable between groups. Wound infection was less frequent after endovascular treatment (0.8% vs 10.9%, p=0.006). Major amputation was independently predicted by CLTI presentation (OR 4.0) and age, not treatment group. Progressive infrainguinal disease, rather than failure of proximal revascularisation, accounted for most amputations in both groups. CONCLUSION: Open bypass confers a substantial mid-term patency and reintervention-free survival advantage over endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, most pronounced in TASC D and CLTI subgroups, without a corresponding difference in limb salvage or survival. These findings support risk-stratified rather than uniformly endovascular-first treatment selection, pending confirmation from the ongoing EVOCC randomised trial.

title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality After Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization (DVA) has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and amputation-free survival (AFS). Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%) (Table 2). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point (Figure 1). All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs 71 years; P = .047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs 47.1%; P = .064) (Table 3). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure. All-cause mortality remained substantial throughout follow-up, consistent with the comorbidity burden of this population. These findings support TADV as a limb-salvage option for patients with no-option CLTI who would otherwise face major amputation, although larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm long-term durability.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. OBJECTIVE: To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. METHODS: Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I= 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. CONCLUSIONS: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

title: Non-General Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for non-general anesthesia (Non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals, and prespecified influence diagnostics. RESULTS: 2 2 Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with general anesthesia (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.54-1.52; I≈86%; wide prediction interval). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for Non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in ICU stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (GRADE). CONCLUSIONS: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to general anesthesia. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

title: Association between increased superficial calcification clusters in carotid atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events after carotid artery stenting: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on CTA. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n=24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n=96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P= 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P= 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P= 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P= 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P= 0.0256, HR= 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P= 0.0265, HR= 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

title: Outcomes of Open vs Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into two groups based on the intervention: EVAR vs OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.25, 95%CI: 0.18-0.34, p<0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95%CI: 0.23-0.42, p<0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95%CI: 0.19-0.31, p<0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the two treatment modalities.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert for detecting peripheral arterial disease in people with suspected intermittent claudication referred to secondary care: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Manual ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI) assessment requires significant time and expertise, precluding its use in primary care. Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended. This study considers the diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert (BVE) in people with suspected intermittent claudication. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional cohort study including people referred to our nurse-led intermittent claudication clinic. BVE measurements were compared to the manual resting ABI/TBI method, using traditional cut-off values of <0.9 and <0.7, respectively. RESULTS: 217 participants and 430 limbs were included, with an overall PAD prevalence of 46%. Sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative predictor values (NPV) for the BVE were 88.5%, 80.7%, 81.3% and 88.1% respectively, when compared to the manual ABI. When compared to the manual TBI, the sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for the BVE were 45.5%, 88%, 62.5% and 78.6% respectively, though this analysis included only 38 limbs. No BVE diagnoses were based on ABI alone, 71% were based on waveform alone and 29% were based on a combination of ABI and waveform. The BVE assessment was significantly quicker to perform than the manual method (p<0.01). CONCLUSION: The BVE demonstrated favourable sensitivity and specificity for detecting or excluding PAD compared to the manual ABI. Further work is needed comparing this device to others, across a range of clinical populations and settings before it can be considered in routine clinical practice.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Exploratory Haemodynamic Numerical Simulation of Patients with Multichannelled Aortic Dissection: A Multicentre, Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multichannelled aortic dissection (MCAD) is a rare type of aortic dissection with limited data on its clinical features and outcomes. This multicentre, retrospective cohort study compared clinical outcomes between MCAD and double channelled aortic dissection (DCAD) and explored haemodynamic differences. METHODS: Patients with aortic dissection were enrolled from three tertiary hospitals. Patients with one true lumen and one false lumen were classified as having DCAD, whereas those with one true lumen and multiple false lumina were classified as having MCAD. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were 30 day and five year all cause mortality after diagnosis. Secondary outcomes included preprocedural mortality, aortic dissection related mortality, post-operative complications, and re-intervention. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Haemodynamic differences were evaluated by exploratory computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis. RESULTS: After matching, 50 patients were included in each group (n = 100). The difference in 30 day mortality was significant (p = .046) and largely reflected preprocedural deaths, which occurred in six patients with MCAD (12%) and none with DCAD (p = .027). Overall survival differed between groups (log rank p = .037; hazard ratio 2.72, 95% confidence interval 1.03 - 7.18; p = .044). Kaplan-Meier estimated mortality at 30 days, one year, and five years was 16%, 23%, and 29% in MCAD compared with 4%, 8%, and 12% in DCAD, respectively. Among treated patients, re-intervention was more frequent in MCAD than in DCAD (21% vs. 6%; p = .036), whereas post-operative complication rates did not differ. Exploratory CFD analysis suggested greater false lumen haemodynamic burden in MCAD. CONCLUSION: MCAD was associated with greater preprocedural mortality and more frequent re-intervention than DCAD. These findings may identify MCAD as a higher risk phenotype warranting closer surveillance and timely evaluation. Haemodynamic observations remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.
